Title: Kinesis Advantage360 Signature Series Custom Keyboard
Body (HTML):
The Advantage360 Signature Series is a build-to-order version of the Kinesis contoured split keyboard. You choose the electronics, the top case color, the switches and the keycaps, and Kinesis assembles the board to that spec. The two halves sit in sculpted key wells, the thumb clusters handle Enter, Space, Backspace and modifiers, and the halves can be spread and tented to suit your shoulders and wrists.

Order it with Pro Bluetooth electronics for wireless use across several devices, or with SmartSet USB electronics for a wired board you program without software. The options below cover the electronics and the top case. Each listing ships with Gateron Brown switches and PBT QWERTY Black keycaps. Kinesis offers more than 150 combinations of switches (Cherry Linear Red, Gateron Brown, Kailh Clicky White, Kailh Quiet Pink) and keycaps, and we can order any of them on request. Custom builds are final sale.

  • Electronics: Pro Bluetooth (wireless) or SmartSet USB (wired)
  • Top case: Black, Gray or White
  • Standard build: Gateron Brown switches with PBT QWERTY Black keycaps
  • More switch and keycap configurations available by request
  • Contoured key wells, split halves with adjustable separation and tenting
  • Built to order by Kinesis; non-returnable

Title: Kinesis FORM Split Keyboard with Touchpad KB100-W
Body (HTML):
FORM is a compact split keyboard from Kinesis with a Windows Precision Touchpad built in between the two halves. It uses a laptop-style key layout, so most people adjust to it quickly, and the split puts your hands at shoulder width. The touchpad lets you point and scroll without reaching for a separate mouse.

The case is machined aluminum and the low-profile mechanical switches have white backlighting. It is a good choice for people who want a split keyboard and a pointing device in one unit.

Title: Kinesis JSB Triple Foot Pedal - Joystick Button Control
Body (HTML):
The Kinesis JSB Triple Pedal is a USB foot switch for Windows that sends joystick button commands rather than keystrokes. Its three pedals are set to joystick buttons 1, 2 and 3, so any program that accepts joystick input can map those buttons to its own functions. That makes it useful for transcription, CAD, gaming, simulation and accessibility setups.

The optional Additional Jack version adds a port for a fourth input, which uses joystick button 4. You can connect a Kinesis single pedal or another compatible switch there. The pedals are full size and solidly built, so you can rest your feet on them.

Rails and adapters like this one are the base of Ergotron's medical accessory system. They let you place scanners, wipes, sharps containers and holders exactly where clinicians need them, and move them later. Send us your cart model and we will put together a complete accessory kit and quote.
